Brazil · scenario outcomes · internal review

What could the outcomes look like?

This view translates each scenario into outcome levels where the project has a matching S0 reference. The main display is an absolute level range—S0 alongside each scenario—rather than a difference alone.

Model status: internal review only. D2 gate v2 is mixed: Tier 1 scenario differences vs S0 PASS; Tier 2 debt/GDP levels FAIL. Debt levels have a historical out-of-sample error of +12.47 pp of GDP against a 5 pp tolerance. Scenario differences are the approved comparison for this gate, but remain model results rather than forecasts.

How to read this

Each row shows an outcome level: S0 and the selected scenario at the chosen horizon. The middle number is the median; the range spans p10 to p90 across model draws.

Red marks a worse direction for that indicator; teal marks a better direction. The meaning depends on the outcome.

S0 is the comparison path: current policy rules continue, while ageing raises pension and health spending. It is a modeled reference, not an observed future or recommendation.

Where the scenario output is a paired difference from S0, this page adds that difference to the displayed S0 level. For distribution indicators and life expectancy, S0 is held flat at the available reference level. The unemployment level is not modeled; its 5.6% anchor is an editable illustration, with a flat S0 assumption.

Infant mortality: the rate is deaths per 1,000 live births. Enter annual births to estimate the number of additional deaths in that year. Without a births count, the page reports the extra deaths per 1,000 births.

These are parameter ranges, not forecast-error ranges. No sourced parameter correlations are used. Only the default package has modeled Gini, poverty, and top-share outcomes; other composition cells are shown as not modeled.

Calculated outcome indicators

GDP level and GDP per capita; debt/GDP with and without C5 feedback; unemployment; infant mortality; life expectancy; HDI health component; adult mean schooling change; Gini; two poverty headcounts; and survey top 1% / top 10% income shares. When an absolute S0 level is not in the model outputs, the page shows only the calculated change vs S0. Model contributions and intermediate fiscal diagnostics are left out.
